title: Training decision models for simulating human respondents
abstract: arXiv:2611.31613v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Researchers increasingly use large language models (LLMs) as synthetic respondents in market research, conjoint analysis, and randomized experiments. However, synthetic choice data from off-the-shelf generative LLMs bias downstream econometric inference. Neither proprietary models nor higher reasoning effort reliably reduces this bias. We investigate decision models (System One architectures) for silicon sampling. Using choice training, we update KEV model weights on historical respondent-level choice microdata by conditional maximum likelihood, before inference and without target-study data. Across three model scales, training on two discrete choice experiments lowers treatment-effect error by 22% to 89% on four held-out studies from new domains (vaccines, nutrition labels, consumer rights, and AI) and new response formats. A small choice-trained model outperforms a much larger off-the-shelf model on three of the four studies. Although

translated_title: 训练决策模型以模拟人类受访者
translated_abstract: 研究人员越来越多地将大型语言模型（LLM）用作市场研究、联合分析和随机实验中的合成受访者。然而，现成的生成式LLM产生的合成选择数据会给下游的计量经济学推断带来偏差，无论是专有模型还是更高的推理投入都无法可靠地减少这种偏差。我们研究了用于硅采样（silicon sampling）的决策模型（System One架构）。通过选择训练，我们在推理之前、不使用目标研究数据的情况下，利用条件极大似然法在历史受访者层面的选择微观数据上更新KEV模型权重。在三个模型规模上，基于两个离散选择实验的训练使四个来自新领域（疫苗、营养标签、消费者权利和人工智能）且采用新回应格式的留存研究的处理效应误差降低了22%至89%。一个经过选择训练的小模型在四个研究中的三个上胜过了规模大得多的现成模型。尽管（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 在历史受访者选择数据上对KEV决策模型进行选择训练，可将LLM合成受访者在跨领域留存研究上的处理效应误差降低22%至89%，且小模型可胜过更大的现成模型。
en_tdlr: Choice-training KEV decision models on historical respondent-level microdata reduces treatment-effect error by 22%–89% on held-out studies from new domains, with a small trained model outperforming a much larger off-the-shelf LLM.
